title: Ten Royal Dharma in Jataka Stories जातककथामा दश राजधर्म
nepali: आजभन्दा २६०० वर्ष अगाडि शाक्यमुनि बुद्धले तत्कालीन घटना र सन्दर्भ जोडेर आफ्नो पूर्व जन्मको घटना बताइएका ५४७ वटा बोधिसत्व जातककथा संग्रह भएको पाइन्छ । ती जातककथाहरूमा राज्यमा सुख, शान्तितथा समृद्धिसहित सुव्यवस्था कायम गर्नको खातिर शासक वर्गले आफनो बानी, व्यवहार तथा कामकर्तव्य पालना गर्ने क्रममा आवश्यक दश गुण वादान, शील, परित्याग, अज्जव, मधव, तप, अक्रोध, अविहिंसा, क्षान्ति र अविरोधी राजधर्मको उल्लेख छन् । बुद्धले तत्कालिन परिस्थितिमा घटेका घटना, परिदृश्य एवम् प्रसंगलाई आफू पूर्व जन्ममा बोद्धिसत्व भएको समयमा घटेका घटनासँग जोड्दै देश नभएको जातककथाहरूमध्ये महाहंस, नन्दियमिगराज, तेलपत, सुमंगल, राजोवाद, कूरू धर्म, जनसंन्ध, भिक्खा परम्परमा दश राजधर्मको उल्लेख भएको पाइन्छ । कुनै कुनै जातकमा अलग-अलग रूपमा र कहीँ न कहीँ अवयव जोडिएर आएको तेसकुश, एकराज, शिवि र वेस्सन्तर जातककथाहरूमा उल्लेख छन् । यसरी जातककथाहरूमा राजाहरूले शासन गरेको घटनालाई जोडी बुद्धकालिन अवस्थाको चित्रण गरेर नैतिक तथा धार्मिक शिक्षा दिएको पाइन्छन् । अतः यो लेखले राज्यमा सुशासन तथा सुव्यवस्था कायम गर्न बुद्ध शिक्षाको महत्व रहेको यथार्थतालाई मध्यनजर राखी जातक कथामा आधारित दश राजधर्मले राज्यमा सुशासन कायम गरेका सन्दर्भ  र ज्ञान वर्तमान अवस्थामा पनि महत्वपूर्ण, सान्दर्भिक र उपयोगी रहेको ज्ञानलाई प्रकाश पारिएको छ ।
american_english: A collection of 547 Bodhisattva Jataka tales is found in which, 2,600 years ago, Shakyamuni Buddha recounted events of his past lives by linking them with contemporary events and contexts. In those Jataka tales, there is mention of the ten royal virtues or qualities—dāna (generosity), śīla (morality), pariccāga (renunciation), ajjava (honesty), maddava (gentleness), tapa (austerity), akkodha (non-anger), avihiṃsā (non-violence), khanti (patience), and avirodha (non-opposition)—necessary for the ruling class in maintaining their habits, conduct, and fulfillment of duties in order to maintain good order along with happiness, peace, and prosperity in the state. While linking events, scenarios, and contexts occurring in the contemporary situation to events occurring during the time he was a Bodhisattva in past lives, the ten royal virtues are found mentioned among the expounded Jataka tales of Mahāhaṃsa, Nandiyamigarāja, Telapatta, Sumaṅgala, Rājovāda, Kuru Dhamma, Janasandha, and Bhikkhāparampara. Mention is made in the Tesakuṇa, Ekarāja, Sibi, and Vessantara Jataka tales, appearing separately in some Jatakas and with interrelated components in others. In this way, by connecting events of kings ruling in the Jataka tales and depicting conditions of the Buddhist era, moral and religious teachings are found to have been imparted. Therefore, keeping in view the reality of the importance of the Buddha's teachings for maintaining good governance and order in the state, this article sheds light on the knowledge that the context and insights of how the ten royal virtues based on Jataka tales maintained good governance in the state remain important, relevant, and useful in the present day as well.

informal_english: You've got a collection of 547 Bodhisattva Jataka stories where, some 2,600 years back, Shakyamuni Buddha shared tales from his past lives by tying them into events and situations happening around him. In those Jatakas, they lay out the ten royal virtues—dāna (generosity), śīla (morality), pariccāga (renunciation), ajjava (honesty), maddava (gentleness), tapa (austerity), akkodha (non-anger), avihiṃsā (non-violence), khanti (patience), and avirodha (non-opposition)—which the rulers really needed to practice in their personal habits and duties to keep peace, happiness, prosperity, and order running smoothly in the country. By tying everyday events and situations back to what happened when he was a Bodhisattva in past lives, the Buddha brings up these ten royal duties across preached Jatakas like Mahāhaṃsa, Nandiyamigarāja, Telapatta, Sumaṅgala, Rājovāda, Kuru Dhamma, Janasandha, and Bhikkhāparampara. They also crop up in the Tesakuṇa, Ekarāja, Sibi, and Vessantara Jatakas, sometimes on their own and sometimes with a few parts tied in here and there, eh. That's how these Jataka tales weave in stories of kings ruling, painting a picture of life in the Buddha's day to deliver solid moral and spiritual guidance. So keeping in mind how important the Buddha's teachings really are for keeping good governance and order, this paper shows that the ways the ten royal duties kept things running smoothly back then are still super important, relevant, and useful today.
